properties.name: muster.mode
properties.description: How far a check goes once a rule is violated: fail-fast stops at the first violated rule, collect-all runs every rule and reports every violation. It configures only the Muster that the starter builds: an application with a Muster bean of its own does not start if it sets it.

properties.name: muster.transaction.reorder-advisor
properties.description: Whether to move the transaction advice one step ahead of Muster's, so that rules run inside the transaction, unless @EnableTransactionManagement has an order of its own. Either way, the application does not start if the transaction advice would not run around Muster's.

properties.name: muster.validation.reorder-advisor
properties.description: Whether to move the method validation advice ahead of Muster's, so that the constraints of a method are checked before its rules and before its transaction, unless the application defines the MethodValidationPostProcessor itself. Off, Spring Boot adds the validation advice last, and the rules run before the constraints.

properties.name: muster.problem-details.mixed-status
properties.description: The status that answers business rule violations of different categories in a Spring MVC application, a client error from 400 to 499. Violations of one category are answered with its status: 403 for forbidden, 404 for not found, 409 for conflict, and 422 for invalid state or no category.

properties.name: muster.rules
properties.description: Switches rules on and off by id, as muster.rules.<rule id>.enabled, for example muster.rules.vehicle.name-unique.enabled=false. Rules are on unless switched off. A key that switches no rule stops the application, and so does any key in an application with a Muster bean of its own.

values.description: Stop at the first violated rule.
Run every rule and report every violation.
